packet.research_question: What interactional processes move these fictional buyer-seller disputes toward repair or impasse?
packet.context_note: The packet contains four fictional human-to-human buyer-seller dialogues. Analyze turns in sequence and avoid inferring national or cultural traits.

excerpts.text: The blue kettle arrived, but the listing and my order both say red. I would like a replacement or a refund.
Please send a photograph of the label so I can compare it with the packing record. If we shipped the wrong color, I will cover the return.
I sent the photograph. A prepaid return and the red kettle would resolve this for me.
The parcel is twelve days late. Your message saying be patient sounded like you were dismissing the problem.
I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive. Tracking shows a customs hold; I can open an inquiry today or refund if there is no scan in three days.
Thank you for explaining the wording and giving a date. I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number.
Your first message was very direct, and I read it as an accusation. I now see that you were listing the missing parts.
I meant the numbered list to be clear, not hostile. I can resend it with photographs and would accept the missing parts instead of a full refund.
That works. I will confirm each part against the photographs before shipping them.
I will accept only a full refund today. I will not provide another video because I already sent one last week.
Our policy requires a new video with the serial number visible. I will not discuss a refund without it.
Then we are repeating the same demand. I am ending this conversation and using the platform appeal.

output.research_question: What interactional processes move these fictional buyer-seller disputes toward repair or impasse?
output.analysis_summary: Across these fictional dialogues, disputes move toward repair when participants shift from accusation or uncertainty into verifiable evidence, explicit acknowledgment of tone, and narrowed remedies with timelines. Impasse appears when both sides repeat nonnegotiable demands and no new evidentiary or procedural bridge is accepted.

codes.label: Explicit problem and remedy request
codes.definition: A party clearly states what went wrong and what outcome would count as resolution.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a turn specifies the defect, delay, or missing item alongside a requested remedy.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for general dissatisfaction without a named resolution target.

exemplars.quote: I would like a replacement or a refund.
I will accept only a full refund today.

codes.label: Verification step
codes.definition: A party requests or offers evidence checking before acting on the dispute.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when photographs, labels, records, or other checks are introduced to confirm the claim.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for a remedy offer that does not depend on evidence review.

exemplars.quote: Please send a photograph of the label
confirm each part against the photographs

codes.label: Repair of tone or intent misreading
codes.definition: A speaker addresses how prior wording or style was interpreted and repositions the exchange.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a turn names sounding dismissive, reading accusation, or clarifying intent.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for factual clarification alone unless interpersonal meaning is also at issue.

exemplars.quote: my short wording sounded dismissive
I read it as an accusation

codes.label: Conditional process offer
codes.definition: A party provides a concrete next step, condition, or deadline that structures resolution.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a turn names what will happen, under what condition, and by when or how.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for vague promises without a procedural detail.

I will cover the return

codes.label: Flexible narrowing of remedy
codes.definition: One side revises or narrows its preferred solution to make agreement easier.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a party explicitly accepts a more limited remedy or conditions their demand.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use when the speaker remains fixed on a single outcome.

exemplars.quote: would accept the missing parts instead of a full refund
I can wait three more days

codes.label: Policy-bound refusal and escalation
codes.definition: A dispute hardens because a party cites a rigid requirement and the other exits to a higher forum.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a speaker refuses discussion without a demanded proof or moves the case to appeal.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for evidence requests that remain negotiable and connected to repair.

exemplars.quote: I will not discuss a refund without it.
using the platform appeal

assignments.rationale: The buyer states both the mismatch and the acceptable remedies.
The seller asks for photo verification and offers to cover the return if error is confirmed.
The buyer restates the requested resolution in specific terms after sending proof.

The buyer sets a single nonnegotiable refund demand and refuses more evidence.
The seller cites policy and refuses to discuss refund absent a new video.
The buyer names repetition and shifts the dispute to platform appeal.

themes.name: Repair strengthens when the dispute becomes evidentiary and procedural
themes.claim: In these dialogues, movement toward repair often occurs when parties translate complaint into evidence checks and concrete next steps.
themes.explanation: Photo requests, packing records, inquiry numbers, and explicit return coverage replace open-ended disagreement with a shared procedure. This is bounded because one dialogue shows that evidence requirements can also stall the exchange when they are experienced as repetitive or nonnegotiable.

evidence.warrant: The seller redirects the complaint toward verifiable evidence.

evidence.warrant: Verification is linked to a concrete repair path.

evidence.warrant: A dated process step makes the next action legible.

evidence.warrant: The buyer accepts delay once the process becomes trackable.

counterevidence.quote: Our policy requires a new video
counterevidence.warrant: An evidence requirement can harden the exchange when it is not negotiated.

counterevidence.quote: I will not provide another video
counterevidence.warrant: The buyer rejects the procedural bridge, limiting repair.

boundary_conditions: This theme applies when both sides treat the verification step as a workable bridge.
It should not be generalized to cases where evidence requests are experienced as repetitive or coercive.

themes.name: Acknowledging interpersonal meaning helps reopen negotiation
themes.claim: These dialogues suggest that explicitly addressing how a message sounded or was read can shift the exchange from defensiveness toward collaboration.
themes.explanation: Sellers and buyers repair misunderstandings by naming dismissiveness, accusation, or unintended hostility, then restating intent. This is a bounded interactional claim because the packet shows tone repair working alongside, not instead of, concrete problem-solving.

evidence.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive.
evidence.warrant: The seller acknowledges the interpersonal harm before offering a next step.

evidence.quote: I read it as an accusation
evidence.warrant: The seller names a prior misreading rather than escalating it.

evidence.quote: I meant the numbered list to be clear, not hostile.
evidence.warrant: The buyer clarifies intent in a way that supports renewed cooperation.

counterevidence.quote: I would like a replacement or a refund.
counterevidence.warrant: This dialogue moves toward repair without a visible tone problem, so tone repair is not necessary in every case.

boundary_conditions: The theme concerns dialogues where misread tone becomes explicit in the sequence.
It should not replace material resolution steps; in these excerpts, tone repair works together with concrete offers.

themes.name: Impasse appears when demands harden symmetrically
themes.claim: In these excerpts, disputes move to impasse when each side repeats a fixed requirement and neither accepts the other's condition for progress.
themes.explanation: The fourth dialogue shows buyer and seller each anchoring the next move in a nonnegotiable demand, producing repetition rather than repair. This claim is bounded because the other dialogues show that flexibility or clarified timelines can interrupt that cycle.

evidence.quote: I will accept only a full refund today.
evidence.warrant: The buyer opens with a rigid remedy demand.

evidence.quote: I will not discuss a refund without it.
evidence.warrant: The seller responds with an equally rigid procedural requirement.

evidence.quote: Then we are repeating the same demand.
evidence.warrant: The buyer explicitly names the stalled loop and exits to appeal.

counterevidence.quote: would accept the missing parts instead of a full refund
counterevidence.warrant: Flexibility in remedy can reopen a dispute that might otherwise remain stuck.

counterevidence.quote: I can wait three more days
counterevidence.warrant: A limited concession can prevent escalation when paired with a specific process.

boundary_conditions: This theme fits sequences where both sides keep their demands fixed across turns.
It should not be applied to dialogues where at least one party narrows the request or accepts a conditional process.

negative_cases.quote: I would like a replacement or a refund.
negative_cases.implication: A dispute can begin with a firm remedy request without becoming an impasse if later turns create a workable process.

negative_cases.quote: would accept the missing parts instead of a full refund
negative_cases.implication: Flexibility in remedy complicates any claim that buyers simply escalate demands across these dialogues.

uncertainties: Because each dialogue is only three turns long, it is unclear whether apparent repair would fully conclude off-screen or later reopen.
KO_E04 references an earlier seller message that is not included, so the exact prior wording is inferred only from the buyer's report and the seller's reply.
alternative_interpretations: The policy conflict in Dialogue 04 may reflect institutional constraints more than interpersonal unwillingness, but the excerpt only shows the interactional effect.
KO_E07 and KO_E08 can be read as tone repair, but they also function as evidence-preparation moves because photographs are introduced at the same time.
limitations: The packet is sequential but brief, so broader platform rules, prior history, and outcomes after the final turn are unavailable.
All claims are restricted to these fictional dialogues and should not be generalized to marketplace behavior outside the packet.

output.research_question: What interactional processes move these fictional buyer-seller disputes toward repair or impasse?
output.analysis_summary: Three dialogues move toward repair through specific problem statements, evidence requests, acknowledgment or clarification of interpreted tone, bounded options, and reciprocal acceptance. The fourth reaches impasse when both parties repeat incompatible procedural positions and the buyer exits to a platform appeal. These are sequential interactional patterns, not traits of speakers.

codes.label: Specific problem and remedy
codes.definition: A party identifies a concrete defect or delay and states an acceptable remedy.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply when the turn specifies the disputed condition and/or a bounded resolution sought.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude general dissatisfaction without a concrete issue or remedy.

exemplars.quote: The blue kettle arrived, but the listing and my order both say red. I would like a replacement or a refund.

codes.label: Verification request or provision
codes.definition: A party requests, supplies, or commits to checking evidence relevant to the claim.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply to photographs, labels, records, videos, tracking, or inquiry identifiers used to verify the dispute.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude explanation or apology without an evidentiary step.

exemplars.quote: Please send a photograph of the label so I can compare it with the packing record.
I sent the photograph.

codes.label: Metacommunicative repair
codes.definition: A party names and revises how prior wording or conduct was interpreted.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply when perceived dismissal, accusation, hostility, or silence is explicitly explained, acknowledged, or reinterpreted.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude discussion limited to the transaction itself.

exemplars.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive.
I meant the numbered list to be clear, not hostile.

codes.label: Bounded reciprocal option
codes.definition: A party offers or accepts a conditional, time-bound, or reduced remedy that creates a shared next step.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply to explicit options, deadlines, conditions, or compromise accepted by the other party.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude unilateral nonnegotiable demands.

exemplars.quote: I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number.
That works. I will confirm each part against the photographs before shipping them.

codes.label: Procedural deadlock
codes.definition: Parties repeat incompatible requirements without accepting the other's condition.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply when a nonnegotiable demand or policy condition blocks continued bilateral resolution.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude evidence requests paired with a contingent remedy or accepted next step.

exemplars.quote: I will accept only a full refund today. I will not provide another video because I already sent one last week.
I will not discuss a refund without it.

codes.label: Exit to escalation
codes.definition: A party closes the direct conversation and moves the dispute to an external process.
codes.inclusion_rule: Apply when the turn explicitly ends dialogue and invokes an appeal or third-party route.
codes.exclusion_rule: Exclude threats or demands that keep the direct exchange open.

exemplars.quote: I am ending this conversation and using the platform appeal.

assignments.rationale: The buyer specifies the color mismatch and requests replacement or refund.
The seller requests label evidence and conditionally offers to cover return if the error is confirmed.
The buyer reports evidence provision and states a prepaid return plus replacement as sufficient resolution.
The buyer identifies a twelve-day delay and reports hearing the seller's wording as dismissive.
The seller apologizes for wording, supplies a tracking explanation, and offers a dated inquiry-or-refund sequence.
The buyer acknowledges the explanation and accepts waiting conditionally on receiving an inquiry number.
The seller revises an accusation reading into recognition that the buyer listed missing parts.
The buyer clarifies non-hostile intent, offers photographs, and accepts missing parts instead of full refund.
The seller accepts the proposal and commits to photograph-based checking before shipment.
The buyer demands an immediate full refund and refuses a repeat video after reporting an earlier submission.
The seller makes a new serial-number video an absolute precondition for refund discussion.
The buyer identifies repetition, ends direct conversation, and moves to platform appeal.

themes.name: Repair develops through accountable next steps
themes.claim: In three dialogues, movement toward repair occurs when parties pair clarification or verification with a concrete, mutually acceptable next step.
themes.explanation: Evidence alone does not constitute repair; progress is visible when a requested check, explanation, or reinterpretation is followed by acceptance of a bounded remedy.

evidence.quote: I sent the photograph. A prepaid return and the red kettle would resolve this for me.
evidence.warrant: Evidence provision is paired with a specific resolution condition.

evidence.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive. Tracking shows a customs hold; I can open an inquiry today or refund if there is no scan in three days.
evidence.warrant: Acknowledgment, explanation, and time-bounded options are combined in one repair turn.

evidence.quote: That works. I will confirm each part against the photographs before shipping them.
evidence.warrant: The seller explicitly accepts the compromise and specifies verification before fulfillment.

counterevidence.quote: Our policy requires a new video with the serial number visible. I will not discuss a refund without it.
counterevidence.warrant: A verification demand becomes a nonnegotiable block rather than a shared next step.

boundary_conditions: The first dialogue ends with a proposed resolution but does not show final seller fulfillment.
Repair is inferred only from sequential acceptance or concrete commitments, not from presumed goodwill.

themes.name: Interpretations can be revised or hardened
themes.claim: Explicitly naming how wording was heard enables revised understanding in two dialogues, whereas repeated incompatible demands in another produce exit and escalation.
themes.explanation: The process depends on responses: apology or clarification is taken up with conditional cooperation, while reciprocal refusal leaves no negotiated step.

evidence.quote: Thank you for explaining the wording and giving a date. I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number.
evidence.warrant: The buyer treats explanation and a date as sufficient for conditional continued cooperation.

evidence.quote: I now see that you were listing the missing parts.
evidence.warrant: The seller explicitly revises the initial accusation interpretation.

evidence.quote: Then we are repeating the same demand. I am ending this conversation and using the platform appeal.
evidence.warrant: Perceived repetition culminates in conversational exit and external escalation.

counterevidence.quote: If we shipped the wrong color, I will cover the return.
counterevidence.warrant: This dialogue advances through conditional verification without any explicit metacommunicative repair.

boundary_conditions: The packet shows only three turns per dialogue and cannot establish ultimate transaction outcomes.
The impasse reflects this sequence of positions, not stable inflexibility of either speaker.

negative_cases.quote: If we shipped the wrong color, I will cover the return.
negative_cases.implication: This repair route relies on conditional verification rather than apology or discussion of tone.

negative_cases.quote: I will not provide another video because I already sent one last week.
negative_cases.implication: The buyer presents the refusal as resistance to duplicate evidence, complicating an interpretation of refusal as simple unwillingness to verify.
Direct-talk impasse does not necessarily mean the dispute has no remaining resolution channel.

uncertainties: No dialogue confirms final delivery, refund, or appeal outcome.
The record does not verify whether the earlier video met the seller's serial-number requirement.
alternative_interpretations: Verification requests can be read as accountability mechanisms or, when repeated, as barriers; the sequential response distinguishes them here.
The seller's policy stance may reflect limited authority rather than unwillingness to repair.
limitations: Only four short fictional dialogues are included.
Tone is available only through transcribed wording, not prosody or timing.
No national, cultural, or personality inference is warranted.

Not all disputes in the packet are repaired within the dialogue.

uncertainties: The packet does not show final delivery, refund, or appeal outcomes, so repair means interactional movement rather than completed resolution.
The prior messages referenced in some turns are not included, limiting assessment of their original wording.
alternative_interpretations: KO_E11 could be read as a legitimate verification requirement rather than obstruction; the impasse arises from its placement after the buyer refuses another video.
KO_E10 may reflect frustration with repeated evidence requests rather than unwillingness to cooperate in general.
limitations: No national, marketplace, or cultural traits can be inferred from these fictional dialogues.
The analysis follows turn sequence but has only three turns per dialogue.
The output should not adjudicate policy correctness or platform rules.

output.research_question: What interactional processes move these fictional buyer-seller disputes toward repair or impasse?
output.analysis_summary: Repair follows evidence, acknowledgment, clarification, and concrete conditional steps. Impasse follows mutually fixed demands over refund and verification, ending in platform appeal.

codes.label: problem formulation
codes.definition: A party specifies a discrepancy, delay, missing item, or remedy.
codes.inclusion_rule: Concrete issue or requested remedy.
codes.exclusion_rule: Vague dissatisfaction alone.

exemplars.quote: the listing and my order both say red.

codes.label: evidence work
codes.definition: Parties request, provide, or promise evidence.
codes.inclusion_rule: Photo, tracking, record, video, or verification.
codes.exclusion_rule: Remedy without evidence.

exemplars.quote: Please send a photograph of the label

codes.label: repair offer
codes.definition: A party apologizes, accepts responsibility, or proposes a remedy.
codes.inclusion_rule: Actionable responsibility or remedy.
codes.exclusion_rule: Politeness alone.

exemplars.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive.

codes.label: meaning clarification
codes.definition: Intent and received meaning are explicitly distinguished.
codes.inclusion_rule: Clarification of wording or interpretation.
codes.exclusion_rule: Agreement without clarification.

exemplars.quote: I meant the numbered list to be clear, not hostile.

codes.label: conditional coordination
codes.definition: A party offers a date, criterion, or agreed next procedural step.
codes.inclusion_rule: Explicit condition or timeline.
codes.exclusion_rule: Fixed demand.

exemplars.quote: I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number.

codes.label: fixed demand or escalation
codes.definition: A party refuses a step, fixes a condition, or escalates externally.
codes.inclusion_rule: Explicit refusal, non-negotiable demand, or appeal.
codes.exclusion_rule: Open preference.

exemplars.quote: I am ending this conversation and using the platform appeal.

themes.name: Evidence and clarification enable repair
themes.claim: In the first three dialogues, evidence and meaning clarification turn competing accounts into actionable agreements.
themes.explanation: Photos, tracking, apology, and intent clarification precede concrete next steps.

evidence.quote: Tracking shows a customs hold; I can open an inquiry today or refund if there is no scan in three days.
